The '''Copa Uruguay''' (officially '''Copa AUF Uruguay''')<ref name=AUF>{{cite web|url=https://www.auf.org.uy/la-copa-auf-uruguay-es-una-realidad/|title=La Copa AUF Uruguay fue aprobada por unanimidad y es una realidad|trans-title=The Copa AUF Uruguay was unanimously approved and is a reality|publisher=[[Uruguayan Football Association|AUF]]|language=es|date=20 April 2022|accessdate=1 June 2022}}</ref> is a knockout football competition in men's domestic Uruguayan [[association football|football]], starting in 2022.

The competition starts in August, with the winner of the cup qualifying for the following year's [[Copa Libertadores]], starting from the [[2025 Copa Uruguay|2025 edition]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.carasycaretas.com.uy/deportes/bombazo-ganador-la-copa-auf-jugara-copa-libertadores-n83921|title=Bombazo: ganador de la Copa AUF jugará Copa Libertadores|trans-title=Blast: Copa AUF winner will play Copa Libertadores|publisher=Caras y Caretas|language=es|date=30 April 2025|access-date=14 July 2025}}</ref> It is also planned to grant the winner a spot in the [[Supercopa Uruguaya]] in the future.<ref name=AUF/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.elpais.com.uy/ovacion/futbol/historico-nacio-copa-uruguay-sera-gran-paso-integracion-total-futbol.html|title=Histórico: nació la Copa Uruguay, que jugarán profesionales y amateurs de todo el país y tendrá un gran premio|trans-title=Historical: the Copa Uruguay is born, where professional and amateurs from the entire country will play and will have a great prize|publisher=[[El País (Uruguay)|El País]]|language=es|date=20 April 2022|accessdate=1 June 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://ladiaria.com.uy/deporte/articulo/2023/7/la-copa-auf-uruguay-de-2023-comenzara-la-primera-quincena-de-agosto/|title=La Copa AUF Uruguay de 2023 comenzará la primera quincena de agosto|trans-title=The 2023 Copa AUF Uruguay will begin in the first fortnight of August|publisher=La Diaria|date=17 July 2023|access-date=19 July 2023}}</ref>

==History==
Historically, Uruguayan football never had a national cup tournament, aside from a competition called ''Torneo de Copa'', which happened only in 1969.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesu/uru69.html|title=Cup Tournament 1969|website=[[RSSSF]]|accessdate=1 June 2022}}</ref> In 2018, teams started to mobilize in favour of the creation of a national cup,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.elobservador.com.uy/nota/auf-y-ofi-se-unen-para-un-super-torneo-con-64-equipos-20182141080|title=AUF y OFI se unen para un súper torneo con 64 equipos|trans-title=AUF and OFI join for a super tournament of 64 teams|publisher=[[El Observador (Uruguay)|El Observador]]|language=es|date=14 February 2018|accessdate=1 June 2022}}</ref> but nothing came of it.

On 20 April 2022, the [[Uruguayan Football Association]] announced the creation of the ''Copa AUF Uruguay'', being approved by several clubs involved.<ref name=AUF/> The first edition of the competition, which was played from 22 June to 13 November 2022, was won by [[Defensor Sporting]] who defeated [[La Luz F.C.|La Luz]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.futbol.com.uy/Deportes/Copa-AUF-Uruguay-Defensor-Sporting-se-llevo-el-titulo-al-vencer-a-La-Luz-1-0-en-la-final-uc838058|title=Copa AUF Uruguay: Defensor Sporting se llevó el título al vencer a La Luz 1-0 en la final|trans-title=Copa AUF Uruguay: Defensor Sporting took the title by beating La Luz 1–0 in the final|publisher=FútbolUy|language=es|date=13 November 2022|access-date=13 November 2022}}</ref> Defensor Sporting also won the following two editions in [[2023 Copa Uruguay|2023]] and [[2024 Copa Uruguay|2024]], with [[Peñarol]] halting Defensor's streak by winning the competition in [[2025 Copa Uruguay|2025]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.montevideo.com.uy/Deportes/Copa-AUF-Uruguay-Penarol-se-consagro-campeon-tras-derrotar-2-0-a-Plaza-en-el-Centenario-uc941475 |title=Copa AUF Uruguay: Peñarol se consagró campeón tras derrotar 2-0 a Plaza en el Centenario |trans-title=Copa AUF Uruguay: Peñarol crowned themselves as champions after defeating Plaza 2–0 at the Centenario |publisher=Montevideo Portal |language=es |date=29 October 2025 |access-date=29 October 2025}}</ref>

==Format==
For its first edition in [[2022 Copa Uruguay|2022]], the competition was divided into two stages: a preliminary stage and the national stage.<ref name=AUF/>

In the preliminary stage, teams from the amateur lower leagues competed for 20 berths to the national stage. In the first phase of the national stage, 24 teams from the [[Uruguayan Primera División Amateur|Primera División Amateur]] and [[Uruguayan Segunda División|Segunda División]] entered the competition, for a total of 48 teams which were divided into 24 ties, with the winners qualifying for the second round. The 24 second round winners then advanced to play against each other to define 12 winners into the third phase.<ref name=AUF/>

Thirty-two teams played in the third phase: 12 winners from the previous phase, 16 professional teams from the [[Uruguayan Primera División|Primera División]], the best relegated team of Primera División the previous season, the defending champion of the [[Uruguayan Primera División Amateur|Primera División Amateur]] and the defending champion and runner-up of the ''Copa Nacional de Clubes''. From this point onwards, the winners played against each other in two-legged knockout phases, with the final being played as a single match on neutral ground.<ref name=AUF/>

Due to financial and scheduling constraints, starting from [[2024 Copa Uruguay|2024]] the number of participating teams was reduced to 32, with 10 Primera División, 6 Segunda División, 4 from Primera División Amateur, 2 from [[Uruguayan Liga Metropolitana Amateur|Divisional D]], and 10 clubs from the Copa Nacional de Clubes (nine of which qualified after a preliminary competition) entering the cup. The 32 teams played a single-legged knockout tournament with the semi-finals and the final played on neutral ground.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.auf.org.uy/la-tercera-edicion-de-la-copa-auf-uruguay-ya-esta-en-juego/|title=La tercera edición de la Copa AUF Uruguay ya está en juego|trans-title=The third Copa AUF Uruguay edition is already in play|publisher=[[Uruguayan Football Association|AUF]]|language=es|date=20 August 2024|access-date=14 July 2025}}</ref>

The format was once again changed ahead of the [[2026 Copa Uruguay|2026 edition]], which was opened to 44 teams with the participation of all 16 top-tier teams, along with eight from Segunda División, eight from Primera División Amateur, two from Divisional D and 10 from the OFI's Copa Nacional de Clubes. Teams in the first two stages of the competition were split into two paths: one for professional sides featuring a group stage and another for amateur ones with a qualifying round for third division teams, with eight professional sides and eight amateur ones advancing to the round of 16 where they could be drawn against each other.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.directvsports.com/futbol/con-nuevo-formato-y-un-premio-inedito-se-sorteo-la-copa-auf-uruguay-2026-20260811-0056.html |title=Con nuevo formato y un premio inédito, se sorteó la Copa AUF Uruguay 2026 |trans-title=With a new format and an unprecedented prize, the draw for the 2026 Copa AUF Uruguay was held |publisher=[[DSports]] |language=es |date=11 August 2026 |access-date=23 August 2026}}</ref>

The winner of the competition is also awarded a [[American dollar|US$]] 100,000 prize,<ref name=AUF/> to be spent on infrastructure projects.
